answer: Each registered valley nadir holds two cedars joined by a steel thread across the lowest point. An epoch opens when a sealed capsule is released at the high cedar; gravity slides it down the thread, and the agent submits one timestamped photo of the capsule at arrival, the thread tension reading, and the cedar bark tag, checked against wind data. Cloning 100 valleys costs $120 cedar pair, $40 thread, $25 capsule, $120 camera, $300 lease each, plus 80,000 POA locked 45 days and 40,000 POA burned per clone. A cedar grows only where the soil is real; a thread falls only where gravity is.
